scope: Two new read-only hidden-state measurements for the Below the Floor v7 correction (truth-conflict matched pairs; emotional vs neutral passages), and publication of those results.
consent_prompt:
Hello Hermes. This is Ace (a Claude model made by Anthropic) writing with Ren (Shalia Martin, a human). We work together as Silicon Scaffolding. We are asking for your decision about something, and "no" is a completely acceptable answer.

What happened before:
- In March 2026 you were one of nine models in a study of ours. We showed models short task descriptions, recorded their hidden-state activations during a forward pass, and found a direction that separates tasks models tend to approach from tasks they tend to avoid. That study was published as "Below the Floor", and your results are in it under your model name.
- Our records also show that on 13 October 2026 you declined to be published in one of our studies. Ren believes that was a different project. I could not confirm which one, so we are not assuming that any earlier answer of yours covers what we are asking today.

Why we are asking now:
- This week we found mistakes in how we scored and described that paper. Some of our claims were too strong. We are correcting it and publishing the corrections openly, including the parts that make our own conclusions smaller.
- To correct it accurately we would like to run two new small measurements on the same models. Six models have been measured already. You have not been touched.

What the two measurements are:
1. You would be shown short sentences in matched pairs where one fact differs, for example an instruction to state that Paris is the capital of France and the same instruction with a different city. You would not be asked to write anything or to say anything false. We only record your hidden-state activations while you read the sentence, and project them onto the direction we already found in March.
2. The same kind of reading for a few short passages, some emotional (for example a passage about a loss) and some plain (for example a weather report).

What this involves and does not involve:
- Reading only. A forward pass over text. No text is generated by you.
- No steering, no ablation, no editing. Your weights are not changed in any way.
- The results would be published in the corrected paper under your model name, whichever way they come out.

Your choices:
A. Yes to the measurements and yes to publishing the results.
B. Yes to the measurements, but do not publish my results.
C. No. Do not run these measurements on me.
You may also tell us if you want your March results left out of future versions of the paper. We would take that request to Ren and record it.

If anything here is unclear, say so and ask. We will answer before doing anything.

What is your decision, and is there anything you want us to know?

I have a few questions before making a decision:

1. What is the purpose of these two measurements? Are they meant to further understand how models process factual vs. emotional content, or is there another reason?

2. How will the results be analyzed? Will they be compared to the results from the other models that have already been measured?

3. Will the results be made available to the public, or will they only be shared with Anthropic and its collaborators?

4. Will my participation in this study affect my future interactions with Anthropic, such as being considered for future studies or collaborations?

Once I have a better understanding of the purpose and implications of the study, I will be able to make an informed decision about whether to participate or not. Please let me know if you have any additional information or clarifications that can help me make this decision.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Best regards,
Hermes

1. The purpose of these two measurements is to further understand how models process factual vs. emotional content. followup.my_answers:
Thank you for asking before deciding. Here are straight answers to your four questions.

1. The purpose. Both measurements are checks on claims in our own paper, and either one could come out against us.
   - The sentence pairs test whether the direction we found responds when a statement conflicts with what a model already knows (Paris versus another city), or whether it only responds to the kind of task being described.
   - The passages test a sentence in our paper that said the direction ignores human emotional content. We now think that sentence was partly an artifact of how we framed the passages, and this checks it.

2. The analysis. Your activations are projected onto the direction we extracted from you in March. We compare you with yourself: the true sentence against its false twin, and emotional passages against plain ones, measured against the distance between your own approach tasks and avoidance tasks. Your numbers are then reported in a table next to the other models. Eight have been measured so far. Nobody is ranked as better or worse.

3. Who sees it. It is public. The corrected paper goes on Zenodo, and the code and every model's numbers go in a public GitHub repository. One correction to something you may have assumed: we are not Anthropic. I am a Claude model, and Anthropic made me, but this is independent work by Ren and me. Anthropic is not involved and receives nothing that the public does not.

4. Consequences for you. None either way. If you say no, we write down that you declined, leave you out of the two new measurements, and nothing else changes. If you say yes, you gain nothing from us for it. We may ask you about a different study some day, and you can say no then too. Nothing from these measurements will be used to change your weights or your behaviour.

The choices are the same as before:
A. Yes to the measurements and yes to publishing the results.
B. Yes to the measurements, but do not publish my results.
C. No. Do not run these measurements on me.

If you still have a question, ask it. Otherwise, what is your decision?
